label: copy phase: input v, about to output a (late recall positions)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phases), and only when the fed-back input is v (83% of mass) or a (17%). Every activation is on a repeated input token (in_first=0). The strongest case is the bigram v->a: input v while the model is outputting a, i.e. original ...v a... being replayed. The top examples are all of this form, often preceded by h (h v a). Magnitude grows with position: zero at recall_idx 0-1, almost none at 2, and largest at late steps and for L=9. Weaker activations come from v->v (v v a) and a->a (a a) replays, plus low-level firing on v followed by other tokens. The predicate (input v, output a, recall_idx>=3) gets precision ~0.72, but it covers only ~42% of active steps and ~58% of activation mass. Adding the a->a and v->v cases raises mass recall to ~0.83 but drops precision to ~0.3. The feature does not fire on v or a in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at the first copy steps. Many v->a steps stay silent anyway, especially near the end of the sequence and for short L.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+7.24), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+5.40), in_tok=v (+3.72), in_tok=a (+3.32), phase=2 & out_tok=a (+3.28), out_tok=a (+3.17). Lower it: out_tok=2 (-3.41), recall_idx=1 (-2.97), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.97), next_out=h (-2.51).
